page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v7 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The memory subsystem delivers 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 472 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and operates without bundled GPU accelerators. Advanced instruction support is comprehensive, featuring AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8).

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core placing in the top 10% (2250.0) and text processing showing top-tier efficiency. Single-threaded data compression also excels, recording strong results in gzip compression (35.65 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.82 GB/sec). Similarly, small-model LLM text generation ranks in the top 25% at 267.16 tokens/sec. Across broader multi-threaded metrics, including PassMark CPU (16576.35) and multi-core Geekbench (8898.0), performance remains squarely within the middle 50% baseline.

Cost efficiency for the D8lds_v7 is driven by its high clock speed, low memory ratio, and integrated NVMe capacity. Because the memory allocation is lower than standard general-purpose tiers (1:2 ratio instead of 1:4), workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools avoid paying for idle memory overhead. The trade-off is memory constraint: while compute throughput and single-core tasks perform well, applications requiring substantial memory buffers or heavy multi-tenant allocations will find the 16.0 GB ceiling restrictive.

The D8lds_v7 is best fitted for compute-intensive workloads that require moderate memory and rely on fast local scratch disk access. Representative use cases include continuous integration and build pipelines (compiling software), web serving tiers, text processing, compression pipelines, and small-model CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory (a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio) and comes bundled with 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without GPU acceleration. The instance excels in single-threaded tasks, placing in the top tiers for Geekbench single-core compute, text processing, and single-threaded gzip compression. While multi-core benchmarks and memory throughput align with standard mid-tier results, the reduced memory footprint provides cost efficiency for workloads that prioritize raw clock speed and low latency local disk over large memory allocations. It is well-suited for code compilation, web application servers, data compression, and lightweight CPU-driven machine learning inference.
